clue.text: It befell at sea, this could help

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing in for the noun

indicators.note: being at sea means confused and all over the place, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these two words, taken as written

explanation.surface: A mishap happened on a voyage, and someone suggests something that might help.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as one story: after an accident at sea, a LIFEBELT is exactly what would help, so the definition is a loose description rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A buoyant ring thrown to someone overboard keeps them afloat, which is the help the phrase has in mind.

clue.text: Second flat dish papa's dropped

indicators.note: something dropped is let fall and lost, so a letter goes missing

parts.note: Papa is P in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone describes a second flat dish that Papa let fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Papa's dropped' reads as a father dropping the dish; really the letter P is dropped from PLATTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Of two things mentioned, the latter is the one named second, so the words are synonyms in that sense.

clue.text: Shows contempt towards loud boors

parts.note: f (forte) is the musical direction for loud

explanation.surface: Noisy oafs being openly disrespectful.
explanation.walkthrough: F for loud comes from musical scores, where forte is marked f.
explanation.definitionFit: To flout a rule or person is to openly disregard them, treating them with scorn.

clue.text: Tanned forehead and tip of nose

indicators.note: the tip of something is its very end, here the leading letter of the word

explanation.surface: A sunbather's forehead and nose tip have caught the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tanned' looks like it describes the forehead, but it is the definition; the rest is simply built up in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Skin that has been tanned by sunshine has turned a darker colour, so it is described with that colour word.

clue.text: Getting behind insulation

definitions.meaning: first meaning: falling back, trailing the others
second meaning: material wrapped round pipes or tanks to keep heat in

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests getting behind some insulation, as in a loft; the two parts are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a present participle of trailing slowly and a noun for heat-retaining wrapping on pipes and boilers.

clue.text: Very good covers for compact masses

parts.note: so means very, as in 'so kind'

explanation.surface: High praise for some lids that keep packed contents in place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very good' looks like one phrase of praise, but it splits: very gives the short intensifier and good describes the covers.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics and everyday speech, solids are substances or bodies with firm, dense structure, as opposed to liquids or gases.

clue.text: Innovative creators saving hour for musicians

indicators.note: to save something is to keep it safely held within
innovative work rearranges the familiar into something new

parts.note: h is the standard abbreviation for hour

explanation.surface: Inventive composers make time for their players.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters split after ORC to take in H, giving ORC-H-ESTRA.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is a large group of instrumental players performing together, so a collective noun for musicians.

clue.text: Lists fashionable Conservative policies

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
a party line is its policy

explanation.surface: Someone enumerates trendy Tory policies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lists' looks like a noun or a verb meaning enumerates; it is the verb for a ship leaning over. Conservative is Britain's main right-of-centre party.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that lists leans to one side, tilting just as a slope tilts from level.

clue.text: Rather cute character turned up with chic clothing

indicators.note: clothing covers and wraps, so one piece is dressed in another
in a down entry, turned up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: the letter T spelt out as a word

explanation.surface: An endearing figure appears wearing stylish clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'character' can mean a letter of the alphabet, and a letter may be spelt out as its name; 'turned up' only works because this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The suffix -ish means 'somewhat', so fairly cute or pleasant is somewhat sweet in the endearing sense.

clue.text: Painstakingly careful from start to finish about records essentially

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round another
the essence of a thing lies at its core, so the central letter is taken

explanation.surface: Someone meticulous checks every record from beginning to end.
explanation.walkthrough: The single middle letter drops in after TH.
explanation.definitionFit: Being thorough means attending to every detail with complete care, exactly what painstaking describes.

clue.text: In computing, integrated circuits lecturer employs initially producing chilly item

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so each word gives its opening letter

parts.words: In computing, integrated circuits lecturer employs
parts.note: the opening letter of each of these six words

explanation.surface: A technical note on how a lecturer uses chips in computer science.
explanation.walkthrough: The long technical preamble is all padding for its initials; 'initially' applies to every word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: An icicle is a hanging spike of frozen water, an object that is cold to the touch.

clue.text: Steak, maybe, generates grumble

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the meat that steak is an example of
second meaning: a complaint, as in 'what's your problem?'

explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' tells you steak is only one example of the first meaning; the second is informal slang for a complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat from cattle includes steak, and in informal English a complaint or grievance is also called by the same short word.

clue.text: Old crossword compiler's admitting figure's large

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one piece is taken inside another

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as I, and 's is short for has: I've
a figure is a number, here ten, plus the S

explanation.surface: A retired setter concedes that a certain body is on the big side.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters refer to themselves as 'I', and 's in 'compiler's' stands for 'has', not a possessive. 'Large' at the end is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extensive covers a wide area or great range, so it is big in extent.

clue.text: Order of ebb and flow reversed around edge of coast

indicators.note: reversed means turned backwards, so the letters run the other way
around means surrounding, so one piece wraps the other
the edge of a word is its outermost letter, here the one at the front

explanation.surface: The sea's rhythm running backwards along the shoreline, as if by command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order of ebb and flow' reads as the sequence of tides; 'Order' alone is the definition, and 'of' only links it.
explanation.definitionFit: An edict is an official decree or proclamation issued by authority, a formal command.

clue.text: Periodically belching, getting something to smoke

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: Someone burping now and then while reaching for a smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: The alternate letters start from the second letter, not the first.
explanation.definitionFit: An electronic cigarette is a battery device used for vaping, a modern alternative to tobacco smoking.

clue.text: By agreement adjusts enclosures round factories

definitions.meaning: first meaning: settles a debt or claim by mutual arrangement
second meaning: fenced areas surrounding industrial buildings

explanation.walkthrough: The first meaning is a legal sense: a creditor may settle a debt for a reduced sum agreed by both sides.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers settling a debt or dispute by mutual terms, and the noun means a walled or fenced area containing buildings.

clue.text: Obese female's parents

explanation.surface: A heavy woman's mother and father.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads the female's parents as her mother and father; the definition keeps only the male ones.
explanation.definitionFit: A father is a male parent, so fathers are an example of parents.

clue.text: Op art — I clearly will frame a very small piece

indicators.note: a frame holds a picture within its borders, so the phrase contains what we want

parts.note: run through these words, ignoring spaces and the dash

explanation.surface: An art critic says an Op Art canvas will surround a tiny fragment.
explanation.walkthrough: Op art is the 1960s style of optical-illusion painting, a natural thing to frame; the answer runs from the P of Op to the start of 'clearly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A particle is a minute portion or fragment of matter, the smallest kind of bit.

clue.text: Remedy ma concocted made an outcry

indicators.note: a concoction mixes ingredients together into something new

explanation.surface: Mother's home-made cure prompted loud complaints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remedy' looks like the definition, but it is part of the letters; the definition is the phrase at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To yammer is to complain loudly or clamour noisily and persistently, so it is a raised protest.

clue.text: Mad Lear distraught and agitated

indicators.note: someone distraught is deeply upset and disordered, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's King Lear raving on the heath, beside himself with grief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad' also looks like an anagram signal, but it is part of the letters; 'distraught' does the shuffling.
explanation.definitionFit: Being alarmed means frightened and disturbed, a state of nervous agitation.

clue.text: Act stopped working at Holyrood

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the Scots form of 'died', as said in Edinburgh

explanation.walkthrough: Holyrood is the seat of the Scottish Parliament in Edinburgh, standing for Scotland; 'stopped working' means died, as a machine or person does.
explanation.definitionFit: A deed is an action performed, and in Scots dialect the past tense of die is spelt this way.

clue.text: Camper's equipment which driver might need to shift?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: kit such as tent and stove

definitions.text: which driver might need to shift?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: what a motorist changes on a manual car

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'shift' has a motoring sense: the driver of a camper van shifting its load becomes changing up or down.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers both general equipment and belongings and the toothed mechanism in a vehicle's transmission selected with the stick.

clue.text: Person who welcomes feminist, entertaining film

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to have them in, so one piece is hosted within another

parts.note: Germaine Greer, author of The Female Eunuch

explanation.surface: A host describes a feminist campaigner who is also showing a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: Germaine Greer is the Australian feminist writer crosswords reach for; ET is the stock short film title.
explanation.definitionFit: A greeter is someone stationed at a door to receive and say hello to arriving guests or customers.

clue.text: Suppose stupid fellow raised bird

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means lifted upward, so the letters read bottom to top

explanation.surface: Imagine that a dim chap had reared a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' suggests bringing up a pet; in a down clue it turns the bird upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: To assume is to take something as true without proof, which is to presume or suppose it.

clue.text: Way of viewing redesigned space over time

indicators.note: a redesign rearranges the parts into a new layout

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An architect's plan for a remodelled room, seen as it changes across years.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'over' means placed above, so the rearranged letters sit on top of T.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspect is a particular angle or perspective from which something is considered, a way of looking at it.

clue.text: Rate eccentric poet, principally melancholy at heart

indicators.note: at heart means in the middle, so this goes inside
eccentric means odd and off-centre, so the letters are arranged unusually
principally means chiefly or first, so the opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: A critic assesses an odd, gloomy poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rate' looks like a verb, to judge the poet; it is the noun for speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempo is the speed at which music is played or things happen, its pace.

clue.text: Works in taxes, drinking beer intermittently

indicators.note: drinking takes something in, so one piece holds another

parts.note: excise is duty on goods such as alcohol

indicators.note: intermittently means on and off, so every other letter is kept

explanation.surface: Someone employed in the tax office who drinks now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Works in taxes' reads as a job; 'Works' alone is the definition, as a verb meaning trains or uses.
explanation.definitionFit: To work a muscle or a faculty is to exercise it, putting it to use and training it.

clue.text: Mate's tableware

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a friend, via Cockney rhyming slang on 'plate'
second meaning: porcelain plates and cups

explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang, 'china plate' rhymes with mate and is shortened to its first word; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyming slang makes the word mean a friend, and fine porcelain dishes are called by the same name after their country of origin.

clue.text: Looking after flipping cooler jewellery

indicators.note: to flip something is to turn it over, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a ring is an item of jewellery

explanation.surface: Someone guarding jewellery that is flippin' cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as the mild British expletive before 'cooler'; it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Caring for someone means tending to their needs and wellbeing, looking after them.

clue.text: Posture of a tense bird you'd picked up

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: to pick up a sound is to hear it, so the words are taken by ear

explanation.surface: Someone describes the stance of a nervous bird they caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' looks like an adjective describing the bird, but it is the grammatical abbreviation; only the last piece is sound-based.
explanation.definitionFit: Attitude can mean a physical bearing or pose of the body, especially in art or ballet.

clue.text: First-born's somewhat cruel destiny

indicators.note: somewhat means to some extent, so only part of the phrase is used

parts.note: the letters run across the gap between these two words

explanation.surface: The firstborn child faces a harsh fate.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after the definition means 'is', joining it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The first-born child in a family is the oldest of the siblings.

clue.text: Reportedly dull exam's most weighty

indicators.note: reportedly means as told by others, so what is heard matters, not the spelling

parts.note: dull as in grey and drab, and an exam as a test

explanation.surface: A boring exam is said to be the most important one.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, the two synonyms run together into a single superlative; the 's means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Great can mean important or serious, so the superlative describes what carries most importance.
